articles.title: ‘Sometimes you just need a good cry’: why Little Women is my feelgood movie
articles.summary: The latest in our series of writers highlighting their go-to comfort films is an ode to the teary 1994 adaptation of the classic novel. I have an ongoing argument with some friends about how I refuse to watch Interstellar again, despite considering it a beautiful and well-crafted film.
body: But at the same time, the movie I choose as my feelgood film is one that has reduced me to a sobbing, snotty mess time and time again, whether I’m watching it curled up with my cat on the couch, swaddled in blankets while sick in bed or jostling with my seatmate for the armrest on an airplane. And just like with the score from Interstellar, the moment I hear Thomas Newman’s wistful little oboe intro of the 1994 version of Little Women, I can feel my eyes well up with tears.

As you’ve probably discerned already, I tend to feel things very strongly. Probably one of my most psychotic traits is that I have to spoil the endings of most movies before I watch them for the first time because if I get too attached to a character and that character dies, it could take me several days to recover. But sometimes you just need a good cry, and that’s exactly what Gillian Armstrong’s Little Women is for me.

articles.title: Bel review – the powerful life force and haunting absence of a traumatised singer-songwriter
articles.summary: Beldina Odenyo alchemised the pain of exile, loss and racism into music as Heir of the Cursed before her death in 2021, as this attentive tribute explores. Instead of an artist in a booth, a lone amplifier plays the music of singer-songwriter Beldina Odenyo for a cluster of microphones to pick up…
body: Performing under the moniker Heir of the Cursed, a translation of the Tetela name of assassinated Congolese leader Patrice Lumumba, Odenyo was on the verge of bigger recognition at the end of 2021 after a successful performance at Edinburgh’s Usher Hall. But hemmed in by successive Covid lockdowns, the 31-year-old is clearly unwell in a discomfiting backstage interview. Squirming, monosyllabic, she seems to be regressing to the non-verbal state of shock in which she arrived in Dumfriesshire from Kenya as a young child.

articles.title: DraftKings Taps Kevin Hart, Nick Jonas for Road-Trip Commercial That Touts Wagering, Predictions
articles.summary: Nick Jonas has been on plenty of road trips — but none quite like this. The actor and musician plays a prominent role in what is expected to be a significant and long-running campaign for sports-wagering giant DraftKings.
body: “We were both kind of kind of dying in the car, and the windows had to be rolled all the way up for it to look the right way for the camera shot,” Jonas recalls. “But we survived.”

And now, the payoff. Fans of NFL and the NBA are likely to see the commercial in various iterations for weeks. The campaign will continue throughout the football and basketball seasons, and DraftKings will also run additional creative featuring Chad Ochocinco and Carmelo Anthony. In addition to the national advertising, DraftKings expects to make promotional forays into local markets as well.

With sports wagering gaining approval in the bulk of the nation, except for 11 states including California, Texas, Georgia and Minnesota, companies like DraftKings and rivals such as FanDuel and BetMGM continue to move aggressively to court sports fans. Football aficionados are likely to encounter the DraftKings pitch week after week, so Jonas and Hart need to demonstrate winning chemistry.

articles.title: The Black Garden review – haunting study of growing up in war-torn Nagorno-Karabakh
articles.summary: Alexis Pazoumian’s documentary follows Samvel and Avo, two preteen boys whose lives will be unavoidably scarred by brutal conflict. After the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, a decades-long territorial dispute exploded in the region of Nagorno-Karabakh, as its largely Armenian population fought…
body: The film opens with the harrowing sight of a bombed-out school in the small village of Talish, where childlike innocence contrasts with wartime trauma. Samvel and Avo, two preteen boys, roam through the wreckage and scavenge for remains of past normalcy, like the scattered notebooks left behind by their former classmates. The threat of the enemy, however, is drilled into every aspect of their daily life. At school, they learn how to assemble guns, and at family gatherings, they join in songs that speak of heroic valour. That the children here – boys and girls – will grow up to become soldiers is a foregone conclusion.
points: Alexis Pazoumian’s documentary follows Samvel and Avo, two preteen boys whose lives will be unavoidably scarred by brutal conflict.

articles.title: Parasomnia review – sleep-schedule horror conjures up a succubus on the loose in waking nightmare
articles.summary: Debut director James Ross II shows promise in this gore fest, but the fear factor suffers from an overly complex plot. Sleep has been part of the horror genre repertoire since The Cabinet of Dr Caligari, and the anxieties around it are spiking as the “ sleep economy ” becomes a thing.
body: The levels of cause and effect, reality and fantasy, in Riley’s dreams are confusing at first: she inhabits the perspective of the eyeball-plucking fiend (a nod to ETA Hoffmann’s Sandman?) and wanders a hellish labyrinth in which past victims are trapped. Thankfully, Ross clarifies everything with a burst of guiding lore in an ingenious third-act switchback that revises the previous two acts.

Despite this sturdy constriction, the film remains only mildly scary – maybe because of the interruptions and vagaries of the complex setup. The middling performances don’t feel extreme enough, and the generic, chalk-faced, taloned bogeyman is a mere stain on Freddy Krueger’s jersey. But there is an undeniable astuteness and agility in the storytelling here on which Ross can build.

articles.title: Naomi Watts to Be Honored at San Sebastián Film Festival
articles.summary: British star Naomi Watts will receive the San Sebastián Film Festival’s prestigious Donostia Award during its 74th edition in September. She joins legendary German director Werner Herzog whose Donostia Award was announced early August. Watts will pick up her Award on Saturday, Sept.
body: British star Naomi Watts will receive the San Sebastián Film Festival’s prestigious Donostia Award during its 74th edition in September.

Born in England, but achieving a career in the U.S. and beyond, Watts broke out in David Lynch’s “Mullholland Drive,” where her performance is “ranked among the finest in contemporary cinema,” said the San Sebastián Festival.
She scored Academy Award nominations for best actress for Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s “21 Grams,” and an Academy Award nomination for J.A. Bayona’s “The Impossible.”

Watts has also worked with Peter Jackson, David Cronenberg, Clint Eastwood, Michael Haneke, Audrey Diwan, Noah Baumbach and Rodrigo García, with whom she came to San Sebastián in 2009 to close the Official Selection out of competition with “Mother & Child.”

articles.title: Rintaro Returns to Korea After 17 Years for Busan’s Japanese Animation Special
articles.summary: The 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) has unveiled a 13-film Japanese Animation Special program, marking the first Korea visit in 17 years for animation master Rintaro alongside four next-generation directors.
body: The lineup’s classics section opens with Yabushita Taiji’s “The White Snake Enchantress” (1958), an adaptation of a Chinese folk tale about a young man who falls for a serpent capable of taking human form. It was the first Japanese animated feature made in full color, and it left a lasting impression on a teenage Miyazaki Hayao, who wrote in “Starting Point 1979-1996” that watching it left him in tears until dawn. The film stands as a landmark work from Toei Animation.

Yamamoto Eiichi’s “Belladonna of Sadness” (1973) was produced by Mushi Production as an experimental work aimed at adult viewers. Adapted from Jules Michelet’s “La Sorcière,” the story centers on Jeanne, a woman who strikes a bargain with the Devil and emerges transformed into a witch. The film was invited to screen at the 1973 Berlin Film Festival, shortly after its debut, and it later became a global cult title following a 2016 4K restoration. Actor Nakadai Tatsuya provides the Devil’s voice, while the camera drifts across static watercolor paintings under Fukai Kuni’s art direction.

articles.title: Dolly Parton laid to rest alongside husband in Nashville
articles.summary: A private family funeral is held for the singer who died on Tuesday at the age of 80.
body: Dolly Parton has been laid to rest, the music legend's great-niece has said.
The singer had a private family funeral in Nashville on Friday, following her death earlier in the week at the age of 80.
She has been placed next to her late husband, Carl Dean, at Woodlawn Memorial Park and Mausoleum in the Tennessee city.

Lainey Parton posted an emotional tribute, external a day after the burial, saying: "It still doesn't feel real that she's gone. I'm going to miss her voice, her laugh, her hugs, and just knowing she was there."

articles.title: Korea Box Office: ‘The Odyssey’ Eclipses ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’
articles.summary: “The Odyssey” held onto the top spot at the South Korean box office during the weekend of Aug. 28–30. According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the Christopher Nolan-directed tentpole generated $8.7 million from 1,058,642 admissions over the three-day…
body: Local family road-trip drama “The Journey to Gyeongju” debuted in third place, generating $912,660 from 124,963 admissions across 801 screens. Directed by Kim Mi-jo, the narrative follows a grieving mother and her three daughters who embark on a journey to Gyeongju to confront the released perpetrator responsible for the death of their youngest family member. Starring Lee Jung-eun, Gong Hyo-jin, Park So-dam, Lee Yeon, and Byun Yo-han, the film has collected $1.3 million from 192,384 total admissions since its Aug. 26 rollout.
“ The End of Oak Street ” opened in fourth place, pulling in $476,938 from 63,472 admissions over the weekend. Since its Aug. 26 arrival, the title has brought $783,473 from 107,438 admissions.

Local animated film “Teenieping: Legend of the Whale Heartstone” finished in fifth place, adding $283,019 from 39,740 admissions. Directed by Kim Soo-hoon, the musical fantasy adventure follows Princess Romi, Heartsping, and their companions exploring an undersea kingdom to rescue Queen Velita. The family film has reached $5.7 million from 838,709 viewers since its Aug. 5 launch.

articles.title: Hints of fiery finale for last ever episode of River City
articles.summary: The Scottish soap opera, based in the fictional Glasgow district of Shieldinch, is coming to an end after 24 years.
body: Johnny McKnight has written for River City for almost a decade so, when it was announced that the show was drawing to a close after 24 years, he asked if he could write the final episode.
"Those moments don't come up very often with long-running shows so I thought it might be cathartic and a nice way to say goodbye as a writer," he says.

Details of the episode, which will air on Monday, are a closely-guarded secret but images released showing a bloodied Lenny Murdoch amidst a dramatic fire scene suggest the show's arch-villain, played by Frank Gallagher, is at the centre of it.
McKnight says he felt a huge responsibility to the show's fans to give them a satisfying ending.

articles.title: In ‘Love Is the Monster,’ Paulina García Is a Granny Facing Impossible Choices (Exclusive TIFF Trailer)
articles.summary: Costa Rican writer-director Neto Villalobos Brenes' dystopian thriller, which world-premieres in Toronto's Centerpiece section and also gets a poster, sees a granddaughter kidnapped for ransom.
body: Love Is the Monster ( Amor es el Monstruo ). Costa Rican writer-director Neto Villalobos Brenes ( All About the Feathers, Helmet Heads ) has picked a title for his latest film that will make you sit up straight, deal with questions swirling through your head, or both. The chilling dystopian thriller, starring Paulina García ( Gloria ) and teeming with fear and inequality, will world premiere in the Toronto International Film Festival’s ( TIFF ) Centerpiece strand on Sept. 15.

“She is forced to make choices she never imagined, pushing love, loyalty and survival into increasingly tense territory,” notes a synopsis of the movie that explores family, love, age and class inequality.
Love Is the Monster sees Villalobos Brenes return to Toronto, where his two previous features also debuted.
